strengths: Cover letter opens with a specific, memorable story about biopharma regulatory work—not a generic company compliment
Gap handling is exemplary: explicitly names missing tools (LangGraph, Pinecone, Weaviate) rather than hoping they won't notice
Specific metrics throughout: 100→300 users, tens of thousands of documents, 3 junior engineers mentored
Authentic technical insights in cover letter ('chunking strategy matters more than model size') signal real expertise, not AI-generated fluff
Fortune-200 regulated environment experience differentiates from candidates with only startup/demo experience
Company research evident: references CDW's $21B revenue, 15,000+ employees, and enterprise scale specifically
weaknesses: Missing 3 of 6 explicitly required skills (LangGraph, Pinecone, Weaviate) is significant for a Senior title—acknowledged well but still a gap
Resume bullets could include more outcome metrics: latency improvements, accuracy/retrieval quality scores, cost reductions
Title progression (AI/LLM Consultant → Senior AI/LLM Consultant) may not clearly map to 'Senior AI Engineer' for some reviewers
No mention of production deployment infrastructure (Docker, Kubernetes, cloud platforms) that often accompanies senior AI roles
revision_suggestions: Consider adding 1-2 more quantified outcomes in resume bullets (e.g., 'reduced retrieval latency by X%', 'improved answer accuracy from X% to Y%')
If you have any exposure to Pinecone, Weaviate, or LangGraph—even personal projects or tutorials—consider a brief 'Currently Learning' section to show proactive growth
Add cloud/infrastructure context if applicable (AWS, Azure, GCP, Docker, Kubernetes) since senior roles often require deployment ownership
